title: GfK/NIQ UK Consumer Confidence Barometer — November 2026: the first edition whose fieldwork falls wholly after the Budget
source: EST: nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/consumer-confidence-plunges-11-points-to-24-in-october/, fetched direct 2026-10-25 — the October-2026 barometer release lists the remaining 2026 press-release dates verbatim as 'October 23rd, November 20th and December 18th' (all Fridays). notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-11-05 from proposals/uk-consumer-confidence-2026-11-20.from-uk-consumer-confidence-2026-10-23.json (read in full, now inert). ONE CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSAL: it expected November fieldwork 'roughly Nov 2-14'. The two November windows readable from NIQ primaries both OPEN Oct 30 (2024: Oct 30-Nov 15, n=2,001; 2025: Oct 30-Nov 14, n=2,003), so the 2026 window should run about Oct 29-Nov 13 - one to two days after the Budget (uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28), not a week. That makes 'wholly after the Budget' true but thin: a start on or before Oct 28 would break it. The window also contains the BoE decision (boe-decision-2026-11-05) and closes before UK CPI (uk-cpi-2026-11-18). Why it earns a slot: October printed -24 (-11, fieldwork Oct 1-14), the largest one-month drop since July 2016, with NIQ naming no single driver; the Budget (OBR headroom ~GBP 15bn, no broad-based tax rise, 10y gilt -1.4bp) was received as priced-in. Post-Budget editions rose in 2024 (-21 to -18) and December 2025 (-19 to -17, 'relief that the Budget was less damaging'). Same-day neighbours already on the calendar: uk-retail-sales-2026-11-20, uk-public-sector-finances-2026-11-20. Expected LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no sterling- or rates-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
